sketches.mechanism: The Maybe monad's >>= operator silently propagates Nothing through an entire chain, so one absence cancels every subsequent step without explicit checks.
sketches.resonance: One moment of absence undoes every future that depended on it — loss propagates silently through everything that follows.
sketches.draft:
what_could_have_been :: Maybe a
what_could_have_been =
  Nothing >>= return >>= return >>= return >>= return

sketches.mechanism: A weak reference automatically becomes nil when the object it points to is deallocated — the language zeroes out your hold on something the moment it ceases to exist elsewhere.
sketches.resonance: You held onto someone, but your grip was weak; when they disappeared from the world, your reference quietly became nothing.

sketches.mechanism: The Elvis operator ?: provides a fallback only when the left side is null — it's a syntax for what you settle for when what you wanted is gone.
sketches.resonance: You reach for what was there; when it's already gone, you accept whatever comes after the question mark.
sketches.draft:
val you: String? = null
val what_remains = you ?: you ?: you ?: you
